ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a stalagmite age-growth record curve, with the vertical axis as height (mm) and the horizontal axis as age (kaB.P); the curve shows changes in the height or growth rate of the stalagmite in different ages. On the right side is a stalagmite profile, with multiple growth layers on the profile, and age information such as 15.21, 16.96, 18.29, and 31.44 marked, indicating that stalagmite growth layers can preserve records of environmental change. Then reason: the question stem states that stalagmites are formed when water saturated with calcium carbonate drips from the cave roof to the cave floor, and their formation is affected by water evaporation and cave temperature. The question has already given one environmental element as “temperature”; the other should be related to the source of dripping water and water-volume recharge. Cave dripping water mainly comes from external rainwater recharge, so stalagmites can also indicate precipitation conditions. Therefore the blank should be filled with “precipitation”.
